summary.oneLiner: The 1,024 Blackwell B200 GPUs went live mid-May and were put on revenue, and that single event re-based the P&L: revenue +334% YoY and +64% QoQ, with EBITDA margin expanding 1,450 bps sequentially to 75.2%. Management insists the numbers reflect capacity and operating leverage, not pricing — and explicitly declines to guide on MRR, capex or peak debt. The strategic pitch has shifted from raw GPU rental to a "Sovereign AI" stack where open-weight models running inside the customer's boundary are the product.

Management insists the numbers reflect capacity and operating leverage, not pricing — and explicitly declines to guide on MRR, capex or peak debt. The strategic pitch has shifted from raw GPU rental to a "Sovereign AI" stack where open-weight models running inside the customer's boundary are the product.

| Metric | Q1 FY27 | YoY | Note |
|---|---|---|---|
| Revenue | INR 1,568 mn (~INR 157 cr) | +334% | +64% QoQ; driven by B200 cluster going live and higher utilisation |
| EBITDA / margin | INR 1,179 mn / 75.2% | — | Margin +1,450 bps vs Q4 FY26 |
| PBT | INR 586 mn | — | vs INR 86 mn in Q4 FY26 |
| PAT | INR 439 mn | — | — |
| Order book | not disclosed | — | Mix shifting toward 1–3 year contracted capacity from monthly/on-demand |
| Cash / net debt | Loan outstanding ~INR 450 crores | — | Taken to fund the first lot of B200; will rise with the next lot. Peak debt explicitly not quantified. |
> Interest cost stepped up this quarter because of the B200 funding loan. Data-centre cost is "largely baked in" for existing capacity; the electricity component will keep rising with usage. Revenue mix: India AI mission ~20–21%, international ~37%, balance domestic.
guidance (critical — verify next quarter:
- **Revenue growth:** none given. "we don't provide guidance on MRR. We always advise everyone to look at what we have done in the past rather than predict the future."
- **Margin:** no number, but management asserted current gross/EBITDA margins are "quite sustainable over the medium term and potentially the long term", driven by utilisation and operating leverage.
- **Order book / inflow:** no target. Direction only — increasing share of 1, 2 and 3-year contracts as customers lock in against price rises.
- **Capex / commissioning:** next lot of 1,024 B200 expected "in the next couple of months". Beyond that, plans to add non-flagship Blackwell, B300 and Vera Rubin generations, with no quantum or date. Total FY27 capex and peak debt explicitly refused.
order book & pipeline: Live capacity is ~5,100 GPUs on the platform today, excluding the additional 1,024 B200 expected shortly. The existing fleet is at "quite a maximal utilisation of capacity … pretty much at maximum level compared to any previous quarter", so incremental growth has to come from capacity additions rather than utilisation. Customers are increasingly asking to contract capacity for 1–3 years — partly triggered by the July price increase, where E2E offered to hold current prices in exchange for longer tenure and advances. Management has not decided what share of the fleet should sit on contracted versus spot/on-demand.
segment / subsidiary detail:
- **SovCloud:** an infrastructure subsidiary focused on build-out, intended to hold and contract large-scale clusters. Funding arrangements were flagged in the presentation but management refused detail — "very early days."
- **Delaware (US) entity:** international sales, presence outside India, alliance management and servicing non-India customers.
- **L&T relationship:** explicitly arm's length and two-way — E2E buys data-centre capacity from L&T, L&T buys E2E cloud, and they go to customers jointly. E2E is also looking to offtake compute capacity if L&T builds it.
growth verticals / optionality: The Sovereign AI thesis is the centrepiece: open-weight models are now "very close behind the frontier models", so an enterprise can deploy inside its own boundary and control fine-tuning, data access and model state — removing the risk of "someone sitting a couple of thousand miles away and judging you for how you're going to use your AI." The stack is three layers (AI factory + TIR/Jarvis Labs software + open-weight models) with the customer's own agentic harness on top. Management frames the monetisation as capturing value at each layer rather than renting frontier APIs. Workloads are fungible — training during working hours, inference at night on the same clusters — so no training/inference revenue split was given.
6a. moat & competitive position:
- **Vendor-neutrality on accelerators:** worked with NVIDIA since 2019 and absorbs their open-source tooling, but "we are also open to integrating any accelerated computing platform… We are quite vendor-neutral in that respect" — the answer to the ASIC-threat question.
- **Owning the platform, not just the metal:** the TIR/Jarvis Labs software layer is what management argues converts a commodity GPU into a sticky sovereign deployment; the pushback on price hikes was reframed as customers finding value in "our software and orchestration platform… solutioning and support."
- **Asserted 6-year GPU life cycle:** management repeatedly claims a minimum six-year monetisation window per generation, with older Hopper fleets "continuing to run very strong" — the direct rebuttal to the obsolescence/ROIC challenge. This is an assertion to be verified, not yet evidence.
margins & cost dynamics: The margin expansion is attributed to three things in order: increased utilisation of the existing fleet, operating leverage as scale grows, and only "very moderate" pricing impact. The July price increase covered both GPUs and CPUs, and management was clear it was cost-driven as much as demand-driven: memory prices rose and hit the CPU side harder in percentage terms than GPUs. Where long-term customers pushed back, E2E offered price protection in exchange for 6-month to multi-year contracts plus advances — many accepted. Data-centre electricity cost will scale with usage but "not a very massive percentage."
capex / expansion (watch slippage): The one dated commitment is the next 1,024 B200 lot arriving in the next couple of months. Everything else is directional: more Blackwell including non-flagship SKUs, and expansion into Vera Rubin. Management's stated posture is "both aggressive as well as judicious." Funding for GPUs already announced is "fully arranged and backstopped by debt or internal accruals or previous equity raises." A question on the INR 881.1 cr preferential-issue capex utilisation was deflected to the CFO and not answered with a breakdown.
capital allocation: Debt of ~INR 450 cr funds the first B200 lot and will rise near term; the CFO declined to quantify peak debt for the year. On further equity, management would "let everyone know if and when that happens" — no commitment either way. The CFO's framing of the balance was "we should not be too aggressive or we should not miss the bus, which is the AI bus." No dividend or buyback discussion.
risks & watch-items:
- **Disclosure opacity is the standing risk:** no MRR guidance, no capex number, no peak debt, no customer-mix split, no training/inference split, no SovCloud funding detail. Management's stated reason — "we're quite small for that right now… these become tracking metrics for everyone" — is a choice, and it makes the quarter hard to underwrite forward.
- Fleet already at maximal utilisation means growth is entirely gated on GPU delivery timing.
- Rising debt against assets with a contested useful life; the 6-year life-cycle claim is the load-bearing assumption for ROIC.
- Concentration in the India AI Mission allocation (~20–21% of revenue) whose renewal path management said was still being worked out "in a couple of weeks."
- Memory-driven hardware cost inflation is now hitting input costs directly, not just the market.
management quality / tone: Tarun Dua is consistent and philosophically confident — "it is still day zero of AI", "we have been in this business for 16-plus years", "cycles will continue" — and repeatedly declines to be drawn on forecasts, which is defensible but leaves analysts modelling blind. He answered the hardest questions (ASIC threat, generational obsolescence, price rollback) directly and at length. Several questions were met with "let us build and execute the plans and then put them out there." Nitin Jain flatly refused to quantify peak debt. The tone is unusually unpromotional for a stock that just printed +334% revenue growth.
non-obvious takeaways:
- The price increase was *rolled back and re-timed*, and the resolution was a tenure-for-price trade — that quietly converts spot revenue into contracted annuity, which matters more than the headline hike.
- CPU hardware cost has risen faster than GPU in percentage terms because of memory — an under-discussed input for neoclouds.
- Management explicitly says inference will dominate globally over time but that at ~5,000 GPUs the split is unmeasurable — a useful reminder of how small the base still is.
- SovCloud existing as a separate infrastructure subsidiary with its own funding arrangement is the structural signal to watch; it is where the balance-sheet expansion will show up.

themes.title: Data-Center & AI electrical/cooling buildout
themes.need: AI/data-center capex pulls transformers, switchgear, gensets, HVAC/cooling, optical and cabling AND a new high-margin cooling supply chain. CUMMINSIND flags DC at ~30-35% of domestic powergen with a demand surge since Oct-2025; VENUSPIPES won a ~INR185cr DC-cooling LOI; AEROFLEX building liquid-cooling skids; BLUESTARCO on DC MEP; STLTECH/NETWEB on optical + HPC/AI servers (STLTECH's DC+Enterprise mix hit 21% of Q1FY27 revenue from 1% in FY26 on record INR13,100cr quarterly order intake anchored by a $1.1bn multi-year hyperscaler deal; FY27 EBITDA-margin guide raised 20%->23% and DC+Enterprise mix guide raised 30%->50% of revenue); REDINGTON/DCI/IVALUE on GPU/AI-infra distribution. Q1FY27 added two balance-sheet-scale entrants: HCLTECH is putting up to INR 3,500cr into its own AI-datacenter business with a 50MW long-term ambition ('megawatt isn't the product, it's the anchor'), and RELIANCE disclosed a 168 MW Meta data centre at Jamnagar built on its own balance sheet.
themes.driver: DC cooling LOIs converting (VENUSPIPES, AEROFLEX); hyperscaler/colo India capex (CUMMINSIND gensets, BLUESTARCO MEP); STLTECH's $1.1bn hyperscaler optical-connectivity deal and 2.4x QoQ order-book jump to INR18,618cr; GPU/AI-infra orders.

business_model.title: Positioning (investor deck)
business_model.body:
- Positions itself as India's sovereign provider of advanced cloud GPUs, with 16+ years of operations, listed on NSE since inception as India's first NSE-listed cloud provider, and running GPU cloud since 2018.
- Frames the opportunity as a structurally undersupplied market: global neocloud revenue cited at $25B in 2025 rising to $180B by 2030 and $400B by 2031, with ~80% of neocloud revenue expected from AI inference by 2030.
- Leans on the sovereignty theme — AI reclassified from procurable utility to strategic national infrastructure — with India's 8.33 GW data-centre pipeline (vs ~1.6 GW live) and the 38,000+ GPU IndiaAI Mission as the domestic demand anchor.
- Differentiates on 'Engineering Owned, Not Rented': 100+ in-house engineers build the compute, networking, orchestration and AI software stack rather than reselling third-party platforms.
- Board and leadership bench is presented as a moat — founder-led (MD Tarun Dua, co-founder, director since inception) with independent directors from Blume Ventures and L&T-Cloudfiniti, plus ex-Dell India President Alok Ohrie as Strategic Advisor.

Management's stated reason — "we're quite small for that right now… these become tracking metrics for everyone" — is a choice, and it makes the quarter hard to underwrite forward.
- Fleet already at maximal utilisation means growth is entirely gated on GPU delivery timing.
- Rising debt against assets with a contested useful life; the 6-year life-cycle claim is the load-bearing assumption for ROIC.
- Concentration in the India AI Mission allocation (~20–21% of revenue) whose renewal path management said was still being worked out "in a couple of weeks."
- Memory-driven hardware cost inflation is now hitting input costs directly, not just the market.

non_obvious.title: Non-obvious takeaways
non_obvious.body:
- The price increase was *rolled back and re-timed*, and the resolution was a tenure-for-price trade — that quietly converts spot revenue into contracted annuity, which matters more than the headline hike.
- CPU hardware cost has risen faster than GPU in percentage terms because of memory — an under-discussed input for neoclouds.
- Management explicitly says inference will dominate globally over time but that at ~5,000 GPUs the split is unmeasurable — a useful reminder of how small the base still is.
- SovCloud existing as a separate infrastructure subsidiary with its own funding arrangement is the structural signal to watch; it is where the balance-sheet expansion will show up.

Their framing; conviction medium given no numbers attached. |

qoq_log.title: QoQ change log (fill each quarter)
qoq_log.body:
- **Q1 FY27 (this):** 1,024 B200 Blackwell went live mid-May and on revenue; 5,100 GPUs live. Revenue INR 1,568 mn (+334% YoY, +64% QoQ); EBITDA INR 1,179 mn at 75.2% (+1,450 bps QoQ); PAT INR 439 mn. Debt ~INR 450 cr. July price increase on GPU and CPU, with tenure-for-price protection offered. SovCloud and Delaware subsidiaries described for the first time. No MRR, capex or peak-debt guidance given.
- _Q2 FY27 → check: did the next 1,024 B200 lot land inside the promised "couple of months"; did the 75% EBITDA margin hold with the new capacity ramping; peak debt and total FY27 capex once disclosed; India AI Mission revenue share after the renewal decision; share of capacity moved onto 1–3 year contracts._

other.title: Notable from the deck
other.body:
- [Corporate action] Executed a 10:1 stock split and listed equity shares on BSE in addition to NSE during Q1 FY27, described as broadening the retail and institutional investor base.
- [Subsidiary] SovCloud was incorporated as a wholly owned subsidiary, aligned with the sovereign/private platform offering for regulated and data-residency-bound customers.
- [Leadership] Alok Ohrie, former President & MD of Dell Technologies India (2013-25), joined as Strategic Advisor, alongside further senior hires across business and technology functions.
